text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Thursday morning newspapers:
- Slovenian Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler threatened to resign if parliament failed to amend the nation's constitution in line with European Union requirements by July 15.
- Slovenian parliament on Wednesday rejected a proposal by opposition centre-right Social Democrats to introduce two new state holidays.
- Slovenian soldiers will join an Austrian battalion in September that is part of a United Nations peace-keeping mission in Cyprus.

- Currently 100 kilometers (60 miles) of motorways in Slovenia are under construction with 62 billion tolars ($391.2 million) of investment planned this year, the country's motorway company DARS said.
- The Slovenian blue-chip SBI index surged 7.7 percent on Wednesday recording the highest daily rise to date, while turnover more than doubled, following a relaxation of rules for foreign investors.
- The Social Democrats threatened the government with a vote of no confidence if it failed to present proposals for the 1997 budget to the parliament by July 20.
- Slovenian president Milan Kucan on Wednesday met opera singer Luciano Pavarotti, who is scheduled to hold a concert in Ljubljana on Friday.

- Over 40 percent of secondary school students in Slovenia say they would take up arms to defend their country, compared with just 16 percent surveyed in an opinion poll in 1991. The poll by Ljubljana's Faculty of Social Science showed that 39 percent preferred to defend the country in some other way.
